description: A stereo amplifier built round the gaussian interpolation filter of the S-SMP chip, which dulls the signal as the frequency setting falls

params.text: Steps the filter through its four settings in turn, and the lamp beside it shows which one: red for Loud, green for Weird, blue for Quiet and unlit for Barely Audible
Sets the gain applied to that input before it reaches the chip, up to 6dB
Sets the output level for that side, -128 to 127; below zero the signal is inverted
Sets the frequency the interpolation filter runs at for that side, five octaves either side of C4; lower settings make the signal duller
Passes the input straight to the output with the chip taken out of the path

inputs.text: Scales the left level knob by the voltage here, 10V leaving it untouched, 0V silencing it and negative voltages inverting it
Scales the right level knob the same way; unpatched it reads the left AMP jack
Left signal to be passed through the filter
Right signal to be passed through the filter; unpatched it reads the left input
Sets the left filter frequency at a volt per octave, added to the FREQ-L knob
Sets the right filter frequency at a volt per octave; unpatched it reads the left V/OCT jack

outputs.text: Carries that side of the filtered signal

notes: the four filter settings get progressively duller and quieter, and the module raises its gain to match, so the change in tone is heard without a change in loudness
menu: Loud — the brightest of the four filter settings, and the one the module comes up in
Weird — the second filter setting, whose response colours the signal rather than only dulling it
Quiet — the third filter setting, duller again
Barely Audible — the dullest filter setting, and the one that leaves the lamp unlit

inputs.2:
±10V · continuous · polyphonic

unpatched it reads the left side's AMP jack.
inputs.4:
±5V · continuous · polyphonic

unpatched it reads the left input.
inputs.6:
1V per octave · continuous · polyphonic

unpatched it reads the left side's V/OCT jack.
